title: Open extension of an injective sheaf is acyclic for the proper right-hand map
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and let $A,B,C,D$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $k:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $i:C\hookrightarrow D$ be open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $r:A\to C$ and $p:B\to D$ be proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism] satisfying $pk=ir$. No Cartesian hypothesis is imposed. For every injective sheaf $J$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] [def-sp-injective-resolutions], the higher direct images of its extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] vanish:
$$R^qp_*(k_!J)=0\qquad(q>0),$$
where the higher direct images are those of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

source.place: Tag 0F7B, label lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, proof of case (b), claim R^q f_*(g_!′ J)=0 and geometric-fibre argument; open-immersion specialization

proof.text: Form V = B ×_D C, b = pullback.fst, s = pullback.snd and t = pullback.lift k r hcomm. The pullback equations give tb = k and ts = r. The map b is open, so t is open by IsOpenImmersion.of_comp. The map s is proper by base change. Since ts is proper and s is separated, IsProper.of_comp makes t proper. Its underlying map is closed, so the range of t is closed.

The proved clopen comparison identifies t_!J with t_*J. Direct image preserves injectives because it is right adjoint to the exact inverse image; transport injectivity through this comparison. No claim about injectivity of the underlying abelian sheaf is used.

Positive integral q is a natural successor. Functor.isZero_rightDerived_obj_injective_succ and homologyRightDerivedFunctorPlusObjSingleFunctorIso give zero for H^q(Rs_*(t_!J)[0]); this is the private injective_vanishing helper.

The finite coefficient ring is additive torsion by isAddTorsion_of_finite. Apply the already available module version isIso_baseChange_of_isProper_of_isAddTorsion_ring, recorded under thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below, to the actual pullback square. Exact inverse image commutes with homology and the single functor; these isomorphisms form proper_homology_baseChange. The open-extension composition isomorphism and the fully faithful unit give b^*(k_!J) ≅ t_!J. Thus i^*H^q(Rp_*(k_!J)[0]) is zero by the preceding step.

At an algebraic-closure point x of D in the range of i, lift x through i and use upperStarComp to pull back the vanishing over C. Outside this range, the ranges of k and pullback.fst p x are disjoint: a common point contradicts hcomm and pullback.condition. The existing disjoint-range vanishing theorem gives pullback.fst^*(k_!J) = 0. This zero sheaf is injective, so the same injective_vanishing helper and proper_homology_baseChange make x^*H^q(Rp_*(k_!J)[0]) zero.

Apply the already proved module-valued isZero_of_forall_isZero_upperStar_algClosurePoint. It is the geometric-stalk conservativity criterion applied to the map from zero and the jointly surjective algebraic-closure points, and gives precisely the claimed module higher-direct-image vanishing.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0F7B, case (b). Module-valued proper base change and the proved clopen comparison replace the abelian forgetful and product-equivalence detours; no unit step is bypassed.
